content: 1. Both clarithromycin and levofloxacin can prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring is required, and therapy may need to be modified. 2. Clomipramine and levofloxacin both increase the QTc interval. Close monitoring is necessary, and therapy adjustments should be considered. 3. Levofloxacin increases the levels of clonazepam by reducing its metabolism. This interaction is considered minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 4. Levofloxacin increases the levels of clorazepate by decreasing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, with unknown clinical significance. 5. Clozapine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Corticotropin and levofloxacin both increase the risk of other adverse effects (see comments). Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids may increase the risk of tendon rupture. 8. Cortisone and levofloxacin both increase the risk of other adverse effects (see comments). Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids may increase the risk of tendon rupture. 9. Crizotinib and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended when using drugs that may prolong the QT interval. 10. Crofelemer increases the levels of levofloxacin by inhibiting certain transporters (MRP2 and OATP1A2) in the gut. However, systemic inhibition is unlikely due to minimal absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Dasatinib and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Degarelix and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Desflurane and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 14. Desipramine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 15. Deutetrabenazine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically significant extent. However, certain conditions may increase the risk of torsades de pointes or sudden death when using QT-prolonging drugs (e.g., bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, co-administration with other QT-prolonging drugs, or congenital QT prolongation). 16. Dexamethasone and levofloxacin both increase the risk of other adverse effects (see comments). Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids may increase the risk of tendon rupture. 17. Levofloxacin and diclofenac may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures due to displacement of GABA from brain receptors. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 18. Didanosine decreases the levels of levofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, administer levofloxacin at least 2 hours before or several hours after didanosine. 19. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. An alternative or additional form of birth control may be recommended during concomitant use. 20. Levofloxacin and diflunisal may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures due to displacement of GABA from brain receptors. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 21. Levofloxacin increases the levels or effects of digoxin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Disopyramide and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 23. Dofetilide and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 24. Dolasetron and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Donepezil and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Doxepin and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 27. Dronedarone and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 28. Droperidol and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 29. Efavirenz and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Eliglustat and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Eluxadoline increases the levels of levofloxacin by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Eluxadoline may also increase the systemic exposure of co-administered OATP1B1 substrates. 32. Encorafenib and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 33. Entrectinib and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 34. Epinephrine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 35. Racemic epinephrine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 36. Eribulin and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 37. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate forms) and levofloxacin all prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 38. Escitalopram increases the toxicity of levofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Levofloxacin increases the levels of estazolam by decreasing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 40. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 41. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens, estropipate, and ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 42. Levofloxacin decreases the effects of ethosuximide by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Quinolones have also been reported to increase phenytoin levels in some cases. 43. Levofloxacin and etodolac may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures due to displacement of GABA from brain receptors. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 44. Ezogabine and levofloxacin both increase each other’s toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Slight and transient QT prolongation has been observed with ezogabine, particularly at doses titrated to 1200 mg/day. QT interval monitoring is recommended when ezogabine is prescribed with QT-prolonging agents. 45. Levofloxacin and fenbufen may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures due to displacement of GABA from brain receptors. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 46. Fennel decreases the levels of levofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Levofloxacin and fenoprofen may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures due to displacement of GABA from brain receptors. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 48. Ferric citrate decreases the levels or effects of levofloxacin by drug binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Administer levofloxacin at least 2 hours before or after ferric citrate. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Ferric maltol, ferrous fumarate, ferrous gluconate, and ferrous sulfate all decrease the levels of levofloxacin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. These interactions apply only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 50. Fexinidazole and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Avoid co-administration of fexinidazole with drugs known to block potassium channels or prolong the QT interval. 51. Fingolimod and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Flecainide and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Fluconazole and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 54. Fludrocortisone and levofloxacin both increase the risk of other adverse effects (see comments). Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids may increase the risk of tendon rupture. 55. Fluoxetine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Fluphenazine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 57. Levofloxacin increases the levels of flurazepam by decreasing its metabolism. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. 58. Levofloxacin and flurbiprofen may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures due to displacement of GABA from brain receptors. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 59. Fluvoxamine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Formoterol and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 61. Foscarnet and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. There is also a minor risk of tonic-clonic seizures with this combination, though the mechanism is unknown. 62. Levofloxacin decreases the effects of fosphenytoin by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. Quinolones have also been reported to increase phenytoin levels in some cases. 63. Fostemsavir and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 64. Gadobenate and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 65. Levofloxacin and gemtuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 66. Gepirone and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 67. Gilteritinib and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Givinostat and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. If co-administration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs when initiating therapy, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. 69. Glasdegib and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor for increased risk of QTc interval prolongation. 70. Levofloxacin increases the effects of glimepiride, glipizide, and glyburide by pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. Quinolone antibiotics may cause hyperor hypoglycemia. Gatifloxacin is most likely to cause dysglycemia, while moxifloxacin is least likely. 71. Goserelin increases the toxicity of levofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely, as this combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 72. Granisetron and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 73. Levofloxacin increases the levels of green tea by decreasing its elimination. This interaction is minor, and its clinical significance is unknown. Some quinolones can inhibit the hepatic clearance of caffeine, so caution is advised. 74. Haloperidol and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 75. Histrelin increases the toxicity of levofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely, as this combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 76. Hydrocortisone and levofloxacin both increase the risk of other adverse effects (see comments). Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids may increase the risk of tendon rupture. 77. Hydrocortisone (rectal) and levofloxacin both increase the risk of other adverse effects (see comments). Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids may increase the risk of tendon rupture. 78. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. 79. Hydroxyzine and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 80. Levofloxacin and ibuprofen (oral and IV forms) may increase the risk of CNS stimulation or seizures due to displacement of GABA from brain receptors. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required.
